title: Stepped release fanout with degrading routes and capacity buckets
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Design and implement a release fanout strategy that degrades routing behavior gracefully based on capacity buckets and observed egress bandwidth per region and tenant. The goal is to enable incremental exposure (A/B, shadow, and micro-canary lanes) while ensuring higher-priority tenants remain within SLOs and low-priority traffic is spilled to best-effort paths or queued for later processing.
background: Current rollout primitives support percentage-based canaries and region failover but do not account for per-tenant bandwidth saturation, transient egress constraints, or mixed degraded responses (partial KV cache misses vs full slow path). We saw a recurrence on 2026-02-17 where an aggressive rollout triggered cross-tenant latency spikes in EU-west due to GPU memory oversubscription and network egress throttling.
proposed_solution: Introduce 'capacity buckets' that encode compute+egress budget per region and tenant priority. Implement a routing tier that dynamically maps incoming requests into lanes: green (full route), amber (degraded route: KV-preserve or reduced max_tokens), and red (spillback to fallback model or enqueue). Fanout will progress in steps: shadow -> micro-A/B -> scaled canary -> gradual ramp, with automated checks that degrade routes first (amber) when a bucket is near threshold instead of immediate rollback.
implementation_notes:
- Extend runtime router to accept bucket metadata with fields: budget_tokens_per_minute, egress_limit_mb_per_minute, tenant_priority_rank (all encoded as strings in config).
- Add rate probes that track moving-window egress and latency quantiles by (region, tenant, model_variant).
- Implement spillback handlers: fast-fallback variant, best-effort offline queue, and synthetic-response hedges.
- Ensure KV cache preservation for amber lane where possible (prefix caching, pinning recent keys).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind 'stepped_fanout' toggle in console. 2) Deploy router changes to staging; run synthetic workload tests. 3) Shadow traffic for 48h at 0.1% of production across two tenants. 4) Micro-A/B with 1% traffic for low-priority tenants and 0.1% for high-priority. 5) If no SLO regressions, proceed to staggered ramp with capacity-bucket thresholds. 6) Auto-rollback triggers: sustained p99 latency > SLA for >= 5 minutes OR error-rate spike above 3x baseline for 2m.
monitoring_and_slo_checks:
- New dashboard: capacity_bucket_utilization (per region/tenant), fanout_lane_distribution, spillback_rate, amber_hit_reduction.
- Alerts: bucket_utilization > 85% (warning), >95% (critical); p99 latency regression > SLA + 30ms (critical).
- Automated canary analyzer will compute behavioral deltas (token-efficiency, hallucination rate proxy via scoring endpoint) before ramping.
acceptance_criteria:
- Router honors capacity buckets and moves traffic between lanes when thresholds crossed.
- Amber lane preserves KV cache for at least 80% of amber requests in synthetic replay.
- Spillback path returns consistent fallthrough behavior and produces telemetry labels for every evicted request.
- Auto-rollback fires and recovers to last safe config without manual intervention.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Over-aggressive spilling may drop low-latency but important requests. Mitigation: tenant_priority_rank allows pinning of critical tenants to green lane until human override.
Risk: Metric noise causing oscillation between lanes. Mitigation: use hysteresis windows and median-of-windows smoothing.
Risk: Complexity in onboarding teams. Mitigation: provide console presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) and runbooks.
